'''Danuel Kennedy House Jr.''' (born June 7, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played two seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]] before transferring to the [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M Aggies]]. During his senior season, he was instrumental in the Aggies' first share of a regular-season [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) championship, as well as their run to the Sweet Sixteen in the [[2016 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2016 NCAA tournament]].

==High school career==
House was born in Houston and grew up in the [[Fourth Ward, Houston|Fourth Ward]]. He attended [[Hightower High School]] in [[Missouri City, Texas]]. As a junior, he averaged 13.9 points, 5.4 rebounds, 1.5 steals, 1.1 blocks and 1.3 assists per game and was named All-District 23-5A First-Team honoree. He averaged 26.0 points, 6.2 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.3 blocks and 1.5 steals per game as a senior and was one of 10 finalists for the Guy V. Lewis Award, an award given to the best player in the Greater Houston area. That season, the Hightower Hurricanes finished with an overall record of 29–9 and a Regional championship game berth. House was ranked 15th in the 2012 class by ESPNU 100 and 26th overall by [[Scout.com]]. House committed to Houston over Ohio State, Baylor, Texas, Georgetown, and Kansas.<ref>{{cite web|title=Danuel House|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/19930|website=[[Rivals.com]]|publisher=Rivals.com|access-date=June 27, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==

===Houston (2012–2014)===
House began his collegiate career at [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]], where he averaged 12.4 points per game as a freshman while competing in 33 games with 27 starts. He was named [[Conference USA|C-USA]] Freshman of the Year, the first in school history to receive the honor. In the first round of the [[College Basketball Invitational]], House hit the game-winning shot against Texas with 17 seconds left. As a sophomore, he was the Cougars' leading scorer and rebounder with 19.6 points and 9.4 rebounds per game, and led the team to the conference semifinals. After the 2013–14 season, House left the team after coach [[James Dickey (basketball, born 1954)|James Dickey]] had resigned,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lerner |first1=Danielle |title=Danuel House Jr.'s connection to Houston runs deep |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/rockets/article/Danuel-House-Jr-s-connection-to-Houston-runs-16510408.php |access-date=19 March 2022 |work=Houston Chronicle |date=5 October 2021}}</ref> and the school granted House's immediate release with the stipulation that he not transfer to another Texas school<ref name="transfer">{{cite news |title=Texas A&M lands Houston transfer Danuel House |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/texas-am-lands-houston-transfer-danuel-house/ |access-date=19 March 2022 |work=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>—a condition the NCAA later refused.

===Texas A&M (2014–2016)===
[[File:Danuel House.jpg|thumb|right|House with the Aggies in 2015]]
House transferred to [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] and received a waiver from the NCAA to immediately play rather than sit out a year.<ref name="waiver">{{cite news |title=NCAA grants surprising transfer waiver to new Aggies wing Danuel House |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/danuel-house-texas-am-eligibility-houston-sampson-ncaa-waiver-transfer-cleared-to-play/1kosxdqi038qn1n3wdauxw6iu5 |access-date=19 March 2022 |work=www.sportingnews.com |language=en}}</ref> He averaged 16.2 points per game and earned first-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] honors. House suffered a foot injury near the end of the season and missed the team's final four games. During his senior season, House averaged 15.6 points, 4.8 rebounds and 2.1 assists per game and scored at least 20 points in nine games. For the first three games of the season, House scored a total of 50 points in wins over USC Upstate, Southeastern Louisiana, and Texas A&M-Corpus Christi. The Aggies went to the [[Battle 4 Atlantis]] finals, losing to Syracuse 74–67. Along the way, the Aggies beat former rival Texas and upset No. 10 Gonzaga with House scoring 19 in each contest. The Aggies finished the regular season with 13 wins, sharing the SEC championship with Kentucky. In the [[2016 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], House averaged 17.0 points per game and scored 32 in the championship game against Kentucky, where the Aggies lost 82–77 in overtime. In the first round of the NCAA Tournament, House scored 20 points in 26 minutes to defeat the Green Bay Phoenix 92–65. In the second round, the Aggies faced the #11 seed Northern Iowa Panthers. By the 5:14 mark in the second half, House had not scored any points<ref>{{cite web|title=23 Danuel House|url=http://www.12thman.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2891|website=Texas A&M University Athletics|publisher=Texas A&M University|access-date=June 26, 2016}}</ref> and ended with 22 in a double-overtime game where the Aggies overcame a 12-point deficit with 44 seconds remaining in regulation to win 92–88. It was the largest last-minute comeback in NCAA basketball history.<ref>{{cite web|title=Texas A&M erases 12-point deficit in last 44 seconds, tops NIU in 2OT|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400872229|website=[[ESPN.com]]|publisher=[[ESPN Inc.]]|access-date=June 26, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Washington Wizards (2016–2017)===
After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], House joined the [[Washington Wizards]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jake|last=Whitacre|title=Washington Wizards sign Sheldon McClellan, Danuel House, Kaleb Tarczewski to deals, according to report|url=http://www.bulletsforever.com/2016/6/24/12022918/sheldon-mcclellan-danuel-house-washington-wizards-texas-am-miami-nba-draft|work=BulletsForever.com|publisher=SB Nation|date=June 24, 2016|access-date=June 26, 2016}}</ref> On September 23, 2016, he signed with the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards Finalize Training Camp Roster|url=https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/09/23/wizards-finalize-training-camp-roster|work=MonumentalSportsNetwork.com|date=September 23, 2016|access-date=September 23, 2016|archive-date=March 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330221751/https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/09/23/wizards-finalize-training-camp-roster|url-status=dead}}</ref> House made his NBA debut on November 11, 2016, recording one rebound in 50 seconds of action against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Danuel House 2016-17 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/houseda01/gamelog/2017/|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 30, 2016}}</ref> On November 30, 2016, he was diagnosed with a fracture in his right wrist and was subsequently ruled out for at least six weeks.<ref>{{cite web|first=Chase|last=Hughes|title=WIZARDS ROOKIE HAS WRIST FRACTURE, TO MISS AT LEAST 6 WEEKS|url=http://www.csnmidatlantic.com/washington-wizards/wizards-rookie-has-wrist-fracture-miss-least-6-weeks|website=CSNMidAtlantic.com|date=November 30, 2016|access-date=November 30, 2016}}</ref> On March 1, 2017, he was waived by the Wizards.<ref name=waived>{{cite web|title=Wizards Sign Brandon Jennings|url=https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2017/03/01/wizards-sign-brandon-jennings|website=MonumentalSportsNetwork.com|date=March 1, 2017|access-date=March 1, 2017|archive-date=March 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302114501/https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2017/03/01/wizards-sign-brandon-jennings|url-status=dead}}</ref> House appeared in just one game for the Wizards, as he missed 39 games with the right wrist injury and 10 games on assignment to the [[NBA Development League]] with the [[Delaware Blue Coats|Delaware 87ers]].<ref name="waived" /><ref>{{cite web|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|work=NBA.com|access-date=February 11, 2017|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2017)===
Around the start of training camp, he signed up with the [[Houston Rockets]]. However, he would be one of the players cut from the final roster at the conclusion of preseason on October 15. He would later be assigned to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the newly rebranded [[NBA G League]] afterwards. House would play for the squad throughout the month of November and the beginning of December, averaging 17.7 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game there.

===Phoenix Suns (2017–2018)===
On December 8, 2017, the [[Phoenix Suns]] signed House to a [[two-way contract]] with the team. Throughout the rest of the season, House would split his playing time there between Phoenix and their [[NBA G League]] squad, the [[Northern Arizona Suns]]. House would make his debut with the team a day later, scoring two points and recording a single rebound in 11 minutes of play in a close loss against the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. On December 16, House would score a season-high 8 points in 15 minutes of playing time in a 108–106 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Phoenix Suns vs Minnesota Timberwolves Box Score|url=https://www.nba.com/game/phx-vs-min-0021700434/box-score#box-score|website=NBA.com|date=December 16, 2017|access-date=December 23, 2021}}</ref> House was later assigned to the [[Northern Arizona Suns]] affiliate alongside [[Davon Reed]] on December 28, mainly for healing purposes. House then returned to action on January 5, 2018, recording what was at the time a new season-high 9 points in a loss against the San Antonio Spurs. On February 23, his two-way contract expired, meaning he couldn't be allowed to play for Phoenix again until after the [[NBA G League]]'s first season under its rebranded name concluded.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=scott bordow|number=967099314290941952|title=Danuel House’s two-way contract has expired. Back with NAZ Suns. Could rejoin team after G League season|user=sbordow|date=February 23, 2018|access-date=December 23, 2021}}</ref> Once that happened, he was allowed to return to Phoenix for the rest of the season. On March 30, House recorded a career-high 8 rebounds in a heartbreaking, buzzer-beating loss against the [[Houston Rockets]]. On April 1, House would record a new season-high with 16 points scored alongside 6 rebounds and 3 assists in a 117–107 loss against the [[Golden State Warriors]]. Two days later, House recorded 14 points, 6 rebounds, and a career-high 5 assists in a 97–94 win against the [[Sacramento Kings]]. On April 6, House would put up his first start in the NBA against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. Two days later, House would record career-highs of 22 points and 8 rebounds in a 117–100 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Golden State Warriors vs Phoenix Suns Box Score|url=https://www.nba.com/game/gsw-vs-phx-0021701203/box-score#box-score|website=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2018|access-date=December 23, 2021}}</ref>

===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2018–2019)===
On June 26, 2018, it was revealed that House would play for the [[Houston Rockets]] in the [[2018 NBA Summer League]], in which he started in all five games.<ref name="nba.com">{{cite web|title=Rockets Convert Contract of Danuel House Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-convert-contract-danuel-house-jr|website=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2018|access-date=March 13, 2019}}</ref> On September 21, 2018, House signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Brady|last=Klopfer|title=Warriors sign Danuel House to a one-year deal|url=https://www.goldenstateofmind.com/2018/7/25/17614608/2018-nba-free-agency-golden-state-warriors-sign-danuel-house-to-one-year-deal|website=GoldenStateOfMind.com|date=July 25, 2018|access-date=March 13, 2019}}</ref> The Warriors released him on October 12.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Waive Davis, House Jr., Nunn and Ulis|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/players-waived-20181012|website=NBA.com|date=October 12, 2018|access-date=October 13, 2018}}</ref> He then re-joined the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] (RGV). In 18 games this season for RGV, he averaged a team-high 20.7 points, 4.6 rebounds, 3.8 assists, and 1.3 steals, including 2.8 made 3-pointers per game.

===Houston Rockets (2018–2021)===
On November 26, 2018, the [[Houston Rockets]] announced that they had called up House from their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Rockets Call-Up Danuel House|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/rockets-call-danuel-house|work=NBA.com|date=November 26, 2018|access-date=November 26, 2018}}</ref> but several days later, on December 4, the [[Houston Rockets]] announced that House was waived.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}} Two days later, he was signed to a two-way contract by the Rockets.<ref>{{cite news|title=Rockets Announce Roster Updates|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-announce-roster-updates|work=NBA.com|date=December 6, 2018|access-date=December 6, 2018}}</ref> On January 16, he was sent back to Rio Grande after House turned down Houston's contract offers, both of which revolved around signing a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rockets fill-in starter House Jr. Off to G League|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/25772795/danuel-house-turns-houston-rockets-offer-play-g-league|website=ESPN.com|date=January 16, 2019|access-date=January 16, 2019}}</ref> In 25 games, House averaged 24.8 minutes, 9.0 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 1.0 assists per game, shooting 39.0 percent from three-point range.<ref>{{cite web|first=Brady|last=Klopfer|title=Rockets to convert Danuel House Jr.'s two-way contract|url=https://www.goldenstateofmind.com/2019/3/12/18262843/2019-nba-warriors-rockets-danuel-house-jr|date=March 12, 2019|website=GoldenStateOfMind.com|access-date=March 13, 2019}}</ref>

On March 12, 2019, Jonathan Feigen of the [[Houston Chronicle]] reported that the [[Houston Rockets]] intended to convert House's two-way contract into a standard NBA contract for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Feigen|title=Rockets convert Danuel House's contract for remainder of season|url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Rockets-Danuel-House-contract-rest-season-playoffs-13683178.php|website=Houston Chronicle|date=March 12, 2019|access-date=March 12, 2019}}</ref> On March 13, 2019, [[Daryl Morey]] announced that the contract conversion was official.<ref name="nba.com"/>

On March 15, [[Chris Paul]] was rested against the [[Phoenix Suns]],{{citation needed|date=January 2022}} allowing House to join the starting lineup in his first game back.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}} In 35 minutes of play, House Jr. tied his season-high number of points in one game with 18 points. He collected three rebounds and one steal, shot 50% from three-point range and 54.55% from the field overall.<ref>{{cite web|title=Suns vs. Rockets - Box Score|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401071703|website=ESPN.com|date=March 15, 2019|access-date=March 16, 2019}}</ref>

On June 30, House agreed to a three-year, $11.1 million extension.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}} On November 27, 2019, House scored a career-high 23 points in 34 minutes in a 117–108 win against the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Feigen|title=Rockets surge past Heat, snap losing streak|url=https://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Houston-Rockets-Miami-Heat-game-recap-14868254.php|website=Houston Chronicle|date=November 28, 2019|access-date=December 1, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Heat vs. Rockets - Box Score|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401160901|website=ESPN.com|date=November 27, 2019|access-date=December 1, 2019}}</ref>

On September 11, 2020, it was announced that House had been expelled from the [[2020 NBA Bubble|NBA's bubble]] in [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]] for violating the league's [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] safety guidelines.<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Rockets' Danuel House Jr. booted from bubble for violating safety protocols|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29863933/rockets-danuel-house-season-violating-safety-protocols|work=ESPN.com|date=September 11, 2020|access-date=September 11, 2020}}</ref> House, who had missed two games while the league's investigation was pending, had reportedly had an unauthorized female guest in his hotel room for a span of "multiple hours."<ref>{{cite web|first=Scott|last=Cacciola|title=Rockets' Danuel House Leaves N.B.A. Bubble After Violation|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/09/11/sports/basketball/nba-houston-rockets-danuel-house.html|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=September 11, 2020|access-date=September 11, 2020}}</ref> Furthermore, the NBA determined that House would be sent home and would not play for the rest of the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20 season]].

On December 18, 2021, House was waived by the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rockets Announce Roster Changes|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-announce-roster-changes|website=NBA.com|date=December 18, 2021|access-date=December 18, 2021}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2021–2022)===
On December 23, 2021, House signed a 10-day contract with the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Danuel House Jr. to a 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-danuel-house-jr-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 23, 2021|access-date=December 23, 2021}}</ref>

=== Utah Jazz (2022) ===
On January 6, 2022, House signed a 10-day contract with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jazz's Danuel House: Joining Utah on 10-day deal|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-danuel-house-joining-utah-on-10-day-deal/|url-status=live|access-date=January 6, 2022|website=CBS Sports|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220106214814/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-danuel-house-joining-utah-on-10-day-deal/ |archive-date=January 6, 2022 }}</ref> He signed a second 10-day contract with the Jazz on January 18.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McDonald |first1=Ryan |title=Utah Jazz bring back Danuel House Jr. |url=https://www.deseret.com/2022/1/18/22890010/utah-jazz-bring-back-danuel-house-jr |access-date=January 18, 2022 |work=[[Deseret News]] |date=January 18, 2022}}</ref> House signed a third 10-day contract with the Jazz on January 28.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jazz Sign Danuel House Jr. to 10-Day Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-danuel-house-jr-10-day-contract-1 |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 28, 2022 |date=January 28, 2022}}</ref> On February 11, the team signed him for the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Utah Jazz Sign Danuel House Jr.|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/utah-jazz-sign-danuel-house-jrthe-utah-jazz-have-signed-forward-danuel-house-jr-team-policy-terms|access-date=February 11, 2022|website=Utah Jazz}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2022–2024)===
On July 6, 2022, House signed a two-year, $8.5 million contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Danuel House Jr. Signs with 76ers|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/danuel-house-jr-joins-76ers|website=Philadelphia 76ers|date= July 6, 2022|access-date=July 7, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=76ers Rumors: Danuel House Agrees to 2-Year, $8.5M Contract After P.J. Tucker Deal |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10040614-76ers-rumors-danuel-house-agrees-to-2-year-85m-contract-after-pj-tucker-deal |access-date=July 9, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref>

On February 8, 2024, the 76ers traded House to the [[Detroit Pistons]],<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The @DetroitPistons announced today that the team has acquired guard/forward Danuel House Jr., a 2024 second round draft pick and cash considerations from the Philadelphia 76ers, in exchange for future 2028 second round draft pick.|number=1755674063564140720|user=Pistons_PR|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Sixers trade Danuel House Jr. to Pistons|url=https://www.nba.com/news/pistons-sixers-trade-house-jr|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}}</ref> who subsequently waived him.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Pistons PR|title=The Detroit Pistons announced today that the team has requested waivers on guards Killian Hayes and Joe Harris and forward Danuel House Jr.|number=1755718966348333261|user=Pistons_PR|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}}</ref>
